scope: Proposition 3.4 (Chain property and invariance) of the manuscript “Purely cosmetic surgery on knots in the three-sphere” (preprints/Purely-Cosmetic-Surgery-on-Knots-in-the-Three-Sphere-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 306 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ee916c92b825a868), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 31. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: With the signs of Proposition 3.3, B is an integral chain map. Compatible homotopies of equation data and incidence representatives give integral chain homotopies. The allowed representative homotopies include smooth conjugation- equivariant homotopies of the normalized based holonomy paths, relative to their collapsed endpoints, under the following requirements. Their exact compact supports remain in the specified parts, they persist under ideal convergence away from a support hit, and the equation data do not depend on the incidence mark. At the lens endpoint the test is supported in N′, its two lifts are tensor-paired with the same exterior, and its flat-cap and collapsed-endpoint avoidance holds throughout. The data admit regularization preserving these requirements. The homotopy of the incidence representative need not be small. Near the primary J endpoint the unconstrained equation exclusion requires no additional behavior of the representative.
